header.running_head: The Du'aas Rasulullaah ﷺ Recited When Bidding Farewell

blocks.text: Rasulullaah ﷺ's Words to a Sahabi (RA) who informed him that he intended Leaving on a Journey

Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that a Sahabi (RA) once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! I intend embarking on a journey, so do give me some provision (du'aas). Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "May Allaah make Taqwa your provision." When he asked for more du'aa, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "May Allaah also forgive your sins." "May my parents be sacrificed for you, O Rasulullaah ﷺ!" the Sahabi (RA) said, "Do give me more." Rasulullaah ﷺ obliged, saying, "And may Allaah make it easy for you to acquire good wherever you may be."[^1]
Rasulullaah ﷺ's Words when Bidding farewell to Hadhrat Qataadah Rahaawi (RA) and another Sahabi (RA)

blocks.arabic_text: جَعَلَ اللّٰهُ التَّقْوٰى زَادَكَ وَغَفَرَ ذَنْبَكَ وَوَجَّهَكَ لِلْخَيْرِ حَيْثُمَا تَوَجَّهْتَ
blocks.text:
Hadhrat Qataadah Rahaawi (RA) says, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ appointed me as leader of my people, I held his hand as he bade me farewell. Rasulullaah ﷺ said:
"May Allaah make Taqwa your provision, forgive your sins and lead you towards good wherever you may be"[^2]

blocks.arabic_text: اَللّٰهُمَّ اطْوِ لَهُ الْبُعْدَ وَهَوِّنْ عَلَيْهِ السَّفَرَ
blocks.text:
Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that a man once said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! I wish to undertake a journey, so please give me some advice." Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Ensure that you always adopt Taqwa and recite ('Allaahu Akbar' اَللّٰهُ أَكْبَرُ) when ascending any slope." As the Sahabi (RA) was leaving, Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa saying:
"O Allaah! Shorten the distance for him and make the journey easy for him"[^3]
The Du'aas Rasulullaah ﷺ Recited When Taking Food or Drink and when Wearing clothing

blocks.arabic_text: اَلْحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ (حَمْدًا) كَثِيْرًا طَيِّبًا مُّبَارَكًا فِيْهِ غَيْرَ مَكْفِيٍّ وَّلَا مُوَدَّعٍ وَّلَا مُسْتَغْنًى عَنْهُ رَبَّنَا
blocks.text:
Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) reports that when Nabi ﷺ lifted the tablecloth off the ground (after eating), he would recite:
"All praise that is most abundant, pure and blessed belongs to Allaah but is (of course) insufficient (to praise Him adequately). O our Rabb,
Tabraani and Bazzaar, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.10 Pg.131).
